summary: Nobuchiyo Kotani is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and Otani University under Yuichi Kajiyama, Noritoshi Aramaki, Hajime Sakurabe, and Ichijo Ogawa. He held posts at Otani University Junior College (~1978–2002) and Otani University (~1982–2010).

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is an Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara. His career includes posts as an assistant professor at the University of Toronto and as a professor at Kyoto University.

Nobuhiro Ota is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1991–2001) and has held posts as a research fellow at the University of Tokyo and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2008).

Nobukatsu Komai is a Buddhist studies scholar. He has held positions as a research student at Taisho University, a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpoin, and a researcher at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Tensho Miyazaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2005–2011). He held posts at Toyo University, the University of Tokyo (~2011–2014), and Tokyo University of Agriculture (~2014).

Nobumi Iyanaga is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. His career includes positions as a lecturer at the University of Tokyo and on a research contract at the École française d'Extrême-Orient's Tokyo Centre (2008–2014).
Nobunaga Takasa is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts as an assistant professor at National Institute of Technology, Sendai College, and as a researcher at Rissho University.
Nobuo Otsuka is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Taisho University (~1982–1987), where he also held a position as a researcher.

Nobuyoshi Yamabe is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Otani University, Osaka University under Noritoshi Aramaki, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Agriculture (~2003–2013) and Waseda University (~2013).

Nobuyuki Kaji is a sinology and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1956–1964). He held posts at Koshien Junior College, Koyasan University, Nagoya University (~1974–1983), Osaka University (~1983–1999), Doshisha University (~1999–2006), and Ritsumeikan University (~2006–2011).
Nobuyuki Watase is an Indology scholar who completed his master's degree at Kyoto University (~1965–1968). He subsequently served as an assistant professor at Tokai University (~1974–2011).

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University (~1959–1969) under Genjun Sasaki and Issai Funahashi. He held posts at Otani University (~1969–2002) and at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (1972).

Norbert M. Samuelson was a philosophy and religious studies scholar. He studied at Northwestern University, Hebrew Union College in New York and Cincinnati, and Indiana University. He held a post at Arizona State University (~1998–2022).

Noriaki Hakamaya is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Zuiho Yamaguchi and Shun'ei Hirai. He held posts at Komazawa University, Komazawa Junior College (~1979–1995), and University of Wisconsin-Madison (1981–1983).
Noriaki Inoue is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University from approximately 1949 to 1953 and later served as a professor at Taisho University.
Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku University (~1962–1966). He later held a position as a professor at Bukkyo University from approximately 1993 to 2015.

Norihiko Uchida is a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He held academic posts as an assistant at Osaka University of Foreign Studies and as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo.

Norihisa Baba is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo, where he later served as an associate professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (~2009–2019).

Norio Koyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Shinshu University (~1979–1983) and under Seitatsu Matsunami, later serving as a professor at both Taisho University and the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Noritoshi Aramaki is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao. He held professorships at Osaka University (~1974–1982), Kyoto University (~1982–1999), and Otani University (~1999–2002), and posts at Hamburg and Kyoto Koka.
